title: A finite T0 space is sober
statement: Let $Y$ be a topological space whose underlying set is finite and which is $T_0$: for any two distinct points $y\ne y'$ of $Y$ there is an open subset of $Y$ containing exactly one of them. Then $Y$ is sober: for every irreducible closed subset $Z\subseteq Y$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] there is exactly one point $\eta\in Z$ whose closure $\overline{\{\eta\}}$ in $Y$ equals $Z$.
